title: Unbounded endomorphism-algebra tensor and global Hom adjunction for a vector bundle
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $A$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, meaning locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}$ for a finite integer $r$, viewed in degree zero. Put $B=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O_X}(E)$ with composition multiplication and left evaluation action on $E$. For a right $B$-module $L$, define $V_E(L)$ to be the sheaf associated to $U\mapsto L\otimes_B E(U)$. Use the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-derived-category]. The total left derived functor $F_E=-\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E$ of $V_E$ exists on all of $D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$, takes values in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, and satisfies $F_E(B)\simeq E$. It has right adjoint $G_E$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, computed on a K-injective resolution $K\to I^\bullet$ by the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(E,I^\bullet)$ with right action $f\cdot b=f\circ b$. The functors and the adjunction are $A$-linear and exact for the standard triangulated structures. After restriction of scalars along $A\to B$, there is a natural derived isomorphism $\operatorname{Res}_A G_E(K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,K)$, where global derived Hom is [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] with its $A$-structure restricted from $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, this identifies $H^q(G_E(K))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,K[q])$, including the right $B$-action by precomposition. Here K-injective means that the complex of maps from every acyclic complex into $I^\bullet$ is acyclic.

proof.text: Write $T(C)^n=V_E(C^n)$, $d_T=V_E(d_C)$ for a right $B$-module complex $C$, and $H(J)^n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(E,J^n)$, $d_H(f)=d_Jf$. The right action is $f\cdot b=f\circ b$: $(f\cdot b_1)\cdot b_2=f\cdot(b_1b_2)$. For a homogeneous map $u:T(C)\to J$, define $\widehat u(c)(e)=u(c\otimes e)$. Conversely define $\widetilde v(c\otimes e)=v(c)(e)$; this is balanced since $v(cb)(e)=v(c)(be)$, and extends uniquely through sheafification. These formulas are inverse and commute with restriction maps. For maps of degree $r$, both carry $d_Ju-(-1)^ru d_C$ to $d_J\widehat u-(-1)^r\widehat u d_C$. They therefore identify the complexes of global maps $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}^{\bullet}(T(C),J)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\bullet}(C,H(J))$, naturally in both arguments.

proof.text: The additive functors $T$ and $H$ preserve chain homotopies: applying either functor to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives the same identity. They commute with shifts and cones, because the cone has terms $J^n\oplus C^{n+1}$ and differential matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_J&f\\0&-d_C\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, and both functors preserve finite direct sums and that matrix. Thus they induce exact functors on homotopy categories, and also after exact localization in their targets. Taking degree-zero cycles modulo boundaries in step 1 gives the ordinary homotopy-category tensor--Hom adjunction.

Regard $B$ as the dg category with one object and endomorphism complex $B[0]$. The semi-free replacement theorem gives a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ for every unbounded right $B$-complex. Its semi-free source is homotopically projective, hence K-projective: acyclicity of its Hom complex implies null homotopy of every map to an acyclic complex. If $s:P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between such sources, its inverse in the derived category lifts to $t:P'\to P$ by the K-projective Hom bijection. Injectivity of that bijection, first with source $P$ and then with source $P'$, gives $ts=1$ and $st=1$ in the homotopy category. Consequently $T(s)$ is a homotopy equivalence. Apply the left-derived existence criterion to the exact functor $Q_XT$ of step 2 and this semi-free class. It supplies an everywhere defined exact left derived functor $F_E$, with $F_E(C)=Q_XT(P)$. The complex $B[0]$ itself is semi-free and $T(B[0])\cong E[0]$ by $b\otimes e\mapsto b(e)$, inverse $e\mapsto1\otimes e$. Thus $F_E(B)\simeq E$.

The split graded filtration of a semi-free $P$ identifies each $P^n$ with a direct sum of copies of $B$: choose the graded splittings, so the union is the direct sum of successive free graded quotients. Hence $T(P)^n$ is the corresponding sheaf coproduct of copies of $E$, by $b\otimes e\mapsto b(e)$ on each summand. The bundle $E$ is quasi-coherent by its local finite-free description. Coproduct closure makes every $T(P)^n$ quasi-coherent. Kernel closure gives $Z^n=\ker(d^n)$ quasi-coherent; $d^{n-1}$ factors through $Z^n$ since $d^nd^{n-1}=0$. Cokernel closure applied to $T(P)^{n-1}\to Z^n$ gives $H^n(T(P))$ quasi-coherent. This proves $F_E(C)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for arbitrary $C$, with no boundedness assertion on $P$.

proof.text: Use the small Zariski site of $X$, enlarging the module universe if necessary. The ringed-site resolution theorem gives $K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective for every unbounded complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. A quasi-isomorphism $s:I\to I'$ between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence: its derived inverse lifts to $t:I'\to I$ by the K-injective Hom bijection with target $I$, and injectivity with targets $I,I'$ gives the two inverse identities. The additive functor $H$ preserves this homotopy equivalence. The right-derived existence criterion, applied to $Q_BH$ and the class of K-injectives, therefore produces a functor $G_E:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$ computed by $H(I)$. This is a functor with its actual right $B$-action, because every map, differential, and homotopy used by $H$ commutes with precomposition by $B$. Shifts and cones of K-injectives are K-injective: mapping an acyclic complex into them gives shifts or cones of acyclic Hom complexes. Thus a triangle between K-injective representatives is represented by its actual cone; step 2 shows that $H$ carries it to a cone triangle. Consequently $G_E$ is exact. Restrict this functor to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$.

proof.text:
For $L\in D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$ choose semi-free $P\to L$, and for $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ choose $K\to I$ K-injective. The two localization bijections and step 1 give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(F_E(L),K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O_X)}(T(P),I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)}(P,H(I))=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)}(L,G_E(K)).$$
These bijections are natural: each is induced by localization or by the explicit evaluation maps of step 1; the bijections make the result independent of the chosen comparison maps between resolutions. Thus $F_E\dashv G_E$ on the ambient categories. By step 4 the left adjoint lands in the full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, so the same Hom bijection restricts to the required adjunction there.

source.place: Tag 09LY, lemma-tensor-with-complex-hom-adjoint, resolved Hom calculation; no compactness or self-Ext vanishing used

proof.text: The complex $E[0]$ is K-flat: for any acyclic $N$, its tensor with $E$ restricts on every trivializing open to a finite direct sum of copies of $N$. The kernel/image computation of cohomology is local, and a finite direct sum of exact complexes is exact. Thus $N\otimes E$ is acyclic on $X$, as required by the definition of K-flatness.

By the construction of derived internal Hom, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,K)$ is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I)$. Step 7 and the K-flat/K-injective Hom theorem show that this representing complex is itself K-injective. The definition of global derived Hom therefore computes $R\Gamma$ on this very complex without any further replacement:
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,K)\simeq Q_{\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)}\Gamma(X,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I)).$$
Its degree-$n$ module is exactly $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(E,I^n)$ and its differential is $f\mapsto d_If$. Restrict scalars along $A\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$: this is the underlying $A$-complex of $H(I)$, since the scalar $a$ acts on $E$ as the endomorphism defining $A\to B$. This yields the claimed natural isomorphism in $D(A)$, rather than merely an equality of cohomology groups. The comparison uses the same maps of K-injective representatives, so is natural in $K$.

A degree-$q$ cocycle of $H(I)$ is a map $f:E\to I^q$ with $d_If=0$, equivalently a chain map $E[0]\to I[q]$; the sign in the differential of $I[q]$ does not change the cycle condition. Boundaries are exactly maps null homotopic as such chain maps (multiplying a homotopy by $(-1)^q$ absorbs the shift sign). Hence $H^q(H(I))=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O_X)}(E,I[q])$. The shift $I[q]$ is K-injective, since mapping into it shifts the Hom complex. The K-injective localization bijection gives $H^q(G_E(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,K[q])$. Its naturality in the source sends $f\circ b$ to precomposition by $b$ in the derived category, proving the right $B$-action clause for every positive, zero, and negative $q$.

The scalar map $A\to B$ is central, because every $\mathcal O_X$-linear endomorphism commutes with multiplication by a global scalar. The maps $c\otimes e\mapsto ac\otimes e=c\otimes ae$ and $f\mapsto af=f\circ(a\operatorname{id}_E)$ make the functors $T,H$ and the evaluation bijection $A$-linear. These equalities also hold on complexes, homotopy classes, and the resolved Hom groups in step 6; thus the derived functors and their adjunction are $A$-linear. Exactness of both derived functors was obtained in steps 3 and 5 from the exact homotopy functors of step 2 and the derived-functor criteria. By the triangulated-subcategory theorem with $T=X$, $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ contains $0$, is stable under shifts and is closed under middle terms of distinguished triangles of $D(\mathcal O_X)$, so it is a full triangulated subcategory whose distinguished triangles are the ambient ones with vertices in it. Hence the restriction of $G_E$ to it is exact, and the left functor, whose values lie in it by step 4, is exact as a functor into it. The shift compatibility of the adjunction is the degree-$r$ differential identity in step 1.
